claims.hypothesis: Hierarchical fragmentation of the filament G205.46-14.56 is governed by thermal Jeans instability rather than turbulence.
claims.experiment: Extracted dense structures across Herschel, JCMT, ACA, and ALMA continuum images using Astrodendro and compared MST nearest-neighbor separations with thermal Jeans lengths.
claims.result: Each hierarchical level fragments into nearly equally spaced structures with separations closely matching the thermal Jeans length of the parental structure.
claims.finding: The hierarchical fragmentation observed in filament G205.46-14.56 is dominated by thermal Jeans instability.

claims.hypothesis: The compact quadruple protostellar system in G205.46-14.56-N2 formed via rotational fragmentation of a rapidly rotating core rather than stochastic turbulent fragmentation.
claims.experiment: Mapped 1.3 mm continuum, CO (2-1) outflows, and H2CO velocity gradients across spatial scales, and compared the morphology and kinematics with pure hydrodynamical simulations of rapidly rotating core collapse.
claims.result: The four central protostars form a mirror-symmetric twin binary system with aligned outflows, connected by a bar with streamers, and exhibit H2CO velocity gradients (37 to 120 km s^-1 pc^-1) and beta sin^2(i) (0.06 to 0.61) that increase at smaller radii.
claims.finding: Ordered fragmentation, aligned outflows, and fast differential rotation are inconsistent with stochastic turbulent fragmentation and provide direct observational evidence for rotation-driven fragmentation.

evidence.quote: Velocity fields traced by H2CO emission reveal clear gradients, and the ratio of rotational kinetic energy to gravitational energy increases with spatial resolution, indicating fast differential rotation within the core.

These findings (ordered fragmentation and aligned outflows) are inconsistent with the stochastic expectations of turbulent fragmentation and instead may provide direct observational evidence that rotation-driven fragmentation is a viable pathway for forming compact protostellar multiple systems.

claims.hypothesis: Magnetic fields play a subdominant role during the fragmentation and disk formation of the multiple system in G205.46-14.56-N2.
claims.experiment: Compared the observed morphology of the central quadruple system and connecting bar/streamers with pure hydrodynamical and non-ideal radiation-MHD simulations from Mignon-Risse et al. (2023).
claims.result: The quadruple system shows striking morphological similarity to pure hydrodynamical simulations but differs substantially from non-ideal radiation-MHD models.
claims.finding: Magnetic fields tentatively play a subdominant role during the fragmentation and disk formation process in G205.46-14.56-N2.

evidence.quote: Notably, the observed central quadruple protostellar system (Fig. 4a) shows striking morphological similarity to the multiple systems formed in pure hydrodynamical simulations (Boss 1991; Mignon-Risse et al. 2023) but differs substantially from the outcomes of non-ideal radiation-MHD models (Mignon-Risse et al. 2023).

This comparison tentatively suggests that magnetic fields may play a subdominant role during the fragmentation and disk formation process of the hierarchically structured protostellar multiple system in G205.46-14.56-N2.

why_this_data.value: G205.46-14.56-N2 hosts five embedded protostars with resolved disks and jets, and higher-resolution ALMA CO (2-1) data (twice the angular resolution of Reipurth et al. 2023) plus multi-scale continuum/line data allow a detailed investigation of its outflows and formation mechanism.

evidence.quote: In contrast, all five embedded members of G205.46-14.56-N2 have already formed protostars (Reipurth et al. 2023), making this multiple system a uniquely valuable laboratory for investigating the formation and early dynamical evolution of compact protostellar clusters.
The ALMA CO (2-1) data used in this work have twice the angular resolution of those used in Reipurth et al. (2023), enabling a more detailed investigation of the molecular outflows.

why_this_method.value: Used deconvolved effective radius instead of Astrodendro rms radius because rms radius is smaller than sub-condensation separations; used CASA imfit for elongated structures with axis ratio > 2 because Astrodendro can fail in crowded environments; stacked three H2CO J=3-2 transitions to enhance sensitivity.

evidence.quote: Astrodendro may fail to identify leaves in crowded environments (Kong et al. 2021). To mitigate this issue, we required the dendro-identified structures to have a major-to-minor axis ratio < 2.
After deconvolution, Rdendro is generally smaller than the separations between embedded smaller condensations in our cases; therefore, it is not suitable for fragmentation analysis.
To enhance sensitivity, we stacked data from three H2CO J=3-2 line transitions.

referee_caveats_inferred: In Appendix D, the rotational-to-gravitational energy ratio beta sin^2(i) is computed across all three spatial resolutions (ACA, ACA+TM2, ACA+TM1+TM2) using fixed values of M = 0.95 M_sun and R = 2400 au from the ACA gas mass alone, without including the embedded stellar mass (~6.3 M_sun) or adjusting R and M for the smaller scale cuts, which may artificially inflate beta at higher resolutions.
The comparison with pure hydrodynamical vs MHD simulations (Mignon-Risse et al. 2023) is purely visual/qualitative and does not include direct magnetic field (e.g., dust polarization) measurements.
Outflow masses in Equation C5 depend on CO (2-1) excitation temperature and optical depth, which are not stated in the text.

Details on which three H2CO J=3-2 transitions were stacked and how the stacking was weighted

(2020) is consulted.
